text:
incbot: ALERT: P1 detected  smart-routing oscillation on /v1/generate (eu region). Multiple customers affected; high error-rate for tool-calling flows.
incbot: initial detection at 2026-03-16T09:12:09Z; routing-loop-count=7 in 2m; error-rate +18% over baseline.

oncall-sre: I'm taking the page. Paging runtime and model infra. @eng-runtime @eng-ml @sara please join.

sara: looking at the traces seeing pattern: requests require tool_call, route tries eu-q pool hitting variant redwood-ggml-q4_1 which reports tool_call=true in the capability cache, but the instance actually rejects tool_call at runtime (model responds with "unsupported feature"). Then smart-routing falls back to other regions/variants which also disagree and cycles back.

tom: confirmed. Example trace (abridged):
```
T=09:12:15 route=eu1 -> candidate=redwood-ggml-q4_1 (metadata.capabilities.tool_call=true)
-> instance response: {"error":"tool calling not supported in runtime"}
-> routing fallback to us-east -> candidate=redwood-ggml-fp16
-> candidate metadata says tool_call=true
-> instance returns same error -> back to eu and cycle repeats
```

priya: that's weird the metadata service and the routing capability cache are inconsistent with instance-level capability reporting. Could be a metadata deploy that didn't update the edge caches or a serialization bug in capability flags for quantized variants.

eng-ml: we rolled a model-metadata update last night that changed q4_1 to indicate tool_call=true for testing but forgot to flip the flag on the runtime plugin that actually implements tool-calling for quantized codepath. So metadata says yes, runtime says no.

eng-runtime: thanks. Immediate mitigations: 1) suppress tool_call routing preference for EU routes, 2) pin /v1/generate in eu to a known-good fp16 variant, 3) invalidate capability cache across routing proxies. Which should we run first?

sara: pinning is lowest customer impact. But need to check capacity. csm_leo, any priority customers in EU relying on tool_call?

csm_leo: two customers have production traffic (FinEdge and Merchantly). FinEdge reported live errors in payment-authorize tool flows. Merchantly on lower load but also seeing retries. They want updates.

eng-runtime: running capacity check: eu fp16 spare capacity = 20% (short window). Should be safe to pin for 30-60 minutes while we fix metadata/runtime.

deploy-bot: /deploy routing-pin --route /v1/generate --region eu --variant redwood-ggml-fp16 --note "incident mitigation"
deploy-bot: dry-run OK. estimated effective RPS capacity change: -9%

oncall-sre: execute deploy now.

oncall-sre: /run deploy routing-pin 2323456791
deploy-bot: job 99281 started; target proxies will pick up config in ~30s

priya: I'm pushing an immediate metadata-service rollback for the q4_1 capability flag and adding a forced publish to edge caches. Also adding a quick runtime plugin toggle to enable a compatibility shim to surface capability=true only when instance supports feature.

eng-ml: pushing change to metadata-service: set redwood-ggml-q4_1.capabilities.tool_call=false, max_context=2048, version=2026-03-16T09:14:00Z. Will add CI check to compare metadata vs runtime healthchecks.

eng-runtime: invalidating routing capability cache now: `cachectl invalidate --scope=routing-capability --variant=redwood-ggml-q4_1`

sara: after pin applied and cache invalidated, fallback_count dropped to normal in ~45s. Error-rate for FinEdge dropped from 24% -> 3% for tool_call flows.

csm_leo: notified FinEdge SRE with timeline and that we've pinned them to fp16 for now. They acknowledged and asked for a postmortem.

eng-ml: root cause = metadata-service accidentally promoted a test flag (tool_call=true) for q4_1 without runtime support; compatibility matrix and routing cache didn't detect the mismatch. Contributing factors: no end-to-end validation between metadata and live instance capabilities, and routing cache TTL too long (5m).

priya: temporary mitigations committed:
- routing.pin for eu -> redwood-ggml-fp16 (rollback in 2 hours if stable)
- capability-cache TTL reduced to 30s
- immediate metadata rollback for q4_1 flag
- added runtime healthcheck endpoint to report per-instance capability booleans

eng-runtime: follow-ups planned:
- enforce cache invalidation on metadata-service deploys (one-liner hook)
- add an integration test that spins up a small routing proxy and model shim to validate capability flags before promotion
- implement auto-pinning automation when fallback loops > 3 within 1m

eng-ml: follow-ups:
- CI check to compare metadata.capabilities vs runtime healthcheck on every model release
- disallow test-only capability flags from reaching production metadata tag without explicit opt-in

oncall-sre: customer impact summary for postmortem:
- affected customers: FinEdge (high), Merchantly (medium)
- incident window: 2026-03-16T09:12:09Z -> 2026-03-16T09:17:30Z (mitigated), monitoring until 09:25Z
- observable impact: tool_call flow error-rate peak 24%, increased latencies from fallbacks ~+600ms median
- actions: pinned variants, rolled back metadata, invalidated caches, reduced TTL, notified customers

csm_leo: will add impact notes to customer tickets and coordinate SLA credit discussion if FinEdge requests.

sara: I'm creating the postmortem doc and filling timeline + evidence. Assigned owners: eng-ml (metadata fixes) = tom, eng-runtime (routing automation & cache hooks) = sara, alerts/auto-mitigation = priya, customer comms = csm_leo.

oncall-sre: leaving channel open for 30m then will move to monitoring. If anyone sees recurrence, page immediately.

incbot: INCIDENT STATUS -> MONITORING at 2026-03-16T09:17:30Z
